key_insight: Halide ordering—not just composition—strongly shifts phase stability and can move structural transition temperatures in mixed halide perovskites by up to 100 K.
engineering_relevance: Tuning halide mix and A-site cations offers a practical route to improve thermal stability and phase control in perovskite solar-cell materials.
method: Trained machine-learned interatomic potentials on DFT reference data for mixed Cs/Rb lead halide perovskites.
Ran large-scale hybrid Monte Carlo–molecular dynamics simulations to sample both configurational and vibrational degrees of freedom.
Mapped miscibility gaps and halide site ordering across Br–Cl, Br–I, and Cl–I systems over 200–500 K.
evidence_signal: The simulations show miscibility gaps in all three binary halide systems and a temperature-dependent preference for layered halide ordering, with CsPbBr3yI3-3y transition temperatures shifting by up to 100 K.
watch_item: The conclusions rely on MLIP-driven simulations and DFT training data, so transferability to unmodeled compositions and long-timescale experimental kinetics may need verification.
paper_title: Strong Impact of Halide Ordering on Structural Phase Transitions in Mixed Perovskites
